1) Can you confirm that inference for our tenant can be restricted to EU region-only processing (no cross-border replication) including backups and operator/maintenance activities?

4) Retention: we need a max retention of 30 days for logs and model context; can you certify deletion and provide an evidence timeline and proof-of-deletion artifact?

We will need these answers (and any SCCs redlines) before our legal team opens the purchase order. Attaching our internal compliance checklist as a reference.

Hi Sofie / Laura / team,

Thanks for the clear list. Brief legal/controls summary below — high level first, followed by recommended next steps for procurement.

1) EU-only processing: For Dedicated and Private customers we can enforce processing and storage inside EU regions. For Hosted we provide an EU-only tenancy with contractual commitments and operational controls (data plane in eu-west-1/eu-central-1 as requested). This includes backups and snapshot retention configured in-region. We will include an addendum to the MSA to lock region.

2) Remote subprocessors: Redwood maintains a subprocessor registry. Current monitoring/telemetry vendors have data-handling limited to metadata (metrics, error traces) and we configure them to not receive user content. Some operational tooling (incident diagnostics) historically required ephemeral access from a limited operator set; we mitigate export risk via:
   - SCCs (EU Standard Contractual Clauses) with all relevant subprocessors
   - Application-level encryption with customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) for Private and Dedicated customers so PII is unreadable without your keys
   - Detailed operator role separation and audited access sessions (session recordings, just-in-time elevation)
   - Explicit logging/alerting and a retention cap (we can enforce 30-day retention for logs tied to your tenant)

3) Operator liability and accidental access: Redwood's standard practice is to minimize operator access to ciphertext; where access is required for emergency debugging we require documented authorization, scoped ephemeral access, and audit trails. For enterprise customers we are willing to provide a signed operator affidavit and tighter contractual limits (e.g., only EU-resident operators, no remote access from outside EEA) depending on the deployment model (Private or Dedicated).

4) Deletion proof: We can provide signed deletion attestations and time-stamped proof-of-deletion manifests for tenant-scoped data. For Hosted with customer-managed KMS, immediate revocation of keys is an option for cryptographic erasure; for Dedicated we can provide deletion workflow and a return/verification report.

Next steps (suggested):
- Laura: share Mediclinic's list of highest-risk data types so we can map controls precisely.
- Mediclinic legal (Ilonica): please send any redline requests on the SCCs PDF I attached.
- Redwood ops: Rishi/engineering to confirm whether remote monitoring subprocessors can be fully excluded for this tenancy or limited to EU-resident vendors.

I'll attach SCCs and an EU-only topology diagram for your review.

Regards,
Jonas
Head, Legal Ops — Redwood Inference

Hi all — technical clarifications from the infra team: we can implement an EU-only tenancy for the Mediclinic environment on Hosted (isolated VPC and dedicated model serving cluster). Specific points:

- Subprocessors: the only non-EU subprocessors currently used are for multi-tenant telemetry ingestion and a US-based observability backup. For the isolated tenancy we can disable remote telemetry flows and instead push metrics to an EU-only observability stack.
- Operator access: for the dedicated tenancy we can require operators to use an EU-only bastion (geo-fenced) and enforce MFA + signed just-in-time approvals. Session recordings and keystroke-level audit are available if requested.
- Retention/enforcement: we will implement an automated retention policy (30 days) for tenant logs and provide a signed manifest at deletion time.
